songs.name: I've Been All Around This World

ai_show_review.summary: Acoustic brilliance, soaring Dark Star & rare Master's Bouquet
ai_show_review.blurb: The show opens with a pristine acoustic set that flows into an electric second half highlighted by a flawless China>Rider transition and a soaring Dark Star. Standout performances include Uncle John's Band, New Speedway Boogie and the rare (Gathering Flowers For) The Master's Bouquet. Recording quality is excellent across the primary soundboard source.
ai_show_review.review:
December 26, 1969 at McFarlin Auditorium captures the Dead in a rare sweet spot where their early acoustic charm meets the burgeoning electric fire of ’69. The first set feels like an intimate folk‑rock gathering – Jerry’s warm Strat tone and Phil’s Alembic‑modified bass lay down a relaxed yet inspired foundation while Tom Constanten’s trippy B‑3 organ adds color to numbers like “Little Sadie” and “I’ve Been All Around This World.”  The transition is marked by the iconic “Uncle John's Band,” which slides seamlessly into an electric second half.  Here the band really lifts off: a flawless “China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider” bridge, a soaring, exploratory Dark Star that builds into a rollicking “New Speedway Boogie,” and the soulful climax of “Turn On Your Lovelight.”  The set also features the ultra‑rare (Gathering Flowers For) The Master's Bouquet, making this performance a collector’s gem.  Across all three soundboard sources the audio is crisp – the Warner‑Evans master stands out with silky‑smooth lows and crystal‑clear highs that require little EQ tweaking, delivering the full nuance of the band’s interplay.

Jerry Garcia’s playing is consistently praised for its warm tone and inventive phrasing, both acoustic and electric. Phil Lesh’s bass shines louder than usual, especially during the China/DS segment. Bob Weir’s vocals and harmonies are spot‑on, with his banter adding a “seriously funny” touch that rounds out the show’s charm. Tom Constanten’s organ work drives the second set, while Bill Kreutzmann (Billy) provides solid drumming once he joins in late; Mickey Hart is present but receives no specific commentary. Overall, the performance feels locked‑in and joyous – a quintessential snapshot of the Dead on the cusp of their legendary early‑’70s era.

best_recording.reason: Excellent soundboard capture with crisp lows, crystal‑clear highs, and a complete set that showcases both the acoustic opener and electric highlights.

key_highlights: Magical acoustic first set that transitions smoothly into an electric second half
Flawless China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider segue
Soaring Dark Star with expansive improvisation

song_highlights: I've Been All Around This World

band_performance.Jerry: Warm Strat tone and inventive phrasing throughout, with inspired acoustic picking and soaring solos in Dark Star.
band_performance.Phil: Strong, audible bass presence; Alembic‑modified Gibson EB‑0 shines especially during the China/DS section.
band_performance.Bob: Spot‑on vocals and harmonies; banter described as seriously funny, adding charm to the set.
band_performance.Billy: Late arrival but solid drumming once in, supporting the electric set with steady drive.
